thread.title: Digital Music: Spotify and Pandora Are ‘Stronger Than Perceived’

author: David Marino-Nachison
title: Digital Music: Spotify and Pandora Are ‘Stronger Than Perceived’
text:
Photo: Courtesy Spotify By David Marino-Nachison Aug. 30, 2018 9:52 a.m. ET “Pure-play” digital music companies Spotify Technology (SPOT) and Pandora Media (P) are holding their own against tech giants, a new analysis of app downloads suggests.
In a Wednesday note, Raymond James analysts examined U.S. iOS and Google Play music app download ratings between June 1 and August 28, finding that—leaving off Apple (AAPL) Music—Pandora and Spotify managed the top two spots on both download platforms.
“This reinforces our view that pure-plays have a stronger than perceived competitive position,” they wrote.
Newsletter Sign-up The reason, they say: The concept of “device ubiquity,” which suggests that the pure-play companies offer a better experience across all platforms and devices. Quote: :
[Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Google is strong in smartphones, but has lagged Amazon.com (AMZN) in connected speakers; Amazon is strong in connected speakers, but had poor success in smartphones .…Given our view that household device ownership is likely to be heterogeneous (i.e. different platforms for phones, watches, connected speakers, and connected cars), we continue to believe pure-play services have a stronger competitive position; they are device-agnostic.
More About Barron’s Next Learn more about Barron’s Next The Barron’s Next 50 All of the companies mentioned in this story are Barron’s Next 50 stocks.
Raymond James has “strong buy” ratings on both Spotify and Pandora; the analysts expect Spotify to turn in Q3 subscriber and monthly average user growth at the “high end” of guidance, and interpret Pandora’s recent announcement of new advertising features as a sign that “execution is improving and the advertising recovery is on track.”
Barron’s Jon Swartz recently took a look at another bullish take on Spotify , while Barron’s Next spoke with Pandora’s CEO in July.
